title: Windows Support 1: Desktop & Access Essentials
subject: File Permissions & Client Management
description: Step into the shoes of a Tier 1 Support Tech. You'll solve everyday tickets involving NTFS permissions, Group Policy, file system limitations, and domain connectivity using an evidence-first workflow.
reportOverview: This report evaluates your ability to troubleshoot user-facing issues. Key skills tested: NTFS vs Share permissions, Active Directory group membership, and file system architecture.
evidenceInstructions:
Instructions:
1) Read the user's complaint.
2) Use the initial step to gather evidence (Effective Access, ipconfig, or Disk Management).
3) Diagnose the logic error (Deny vs Allow, FAT32 vs NTFS).
4) Apply the Fix and document the change.

tickets.title: HR New Hire Access Request
tickets.summary: A new employee in HR, Sarah Jenkins, reports she cannot open the 'HR_Private' folder on the shared drive. Other HR staff have no issues.
artifact: Error: 'Windows cannot access \\FileServer\HR_Private - Access is Denied'
AD Check: User is a member of 'Domain Users' and 'HR_Department' groups.
Folder Security: 'HR_Staff' group has Modify permissions; 'HR_Department' is not listed.

triage.q: What is the most efficient way to see exactly why Sarah is being blocked?
options: Ask Sarah to restart her computer three times
Check the 'Effective Access' tab in the folder's Advanced Security settings for sjenkins
Delete the HR folder and recreate it
Give Sarah the Domain Admin password temporarily

diagnosis.q: Sarah is in 'HR_Department' but the folder gives access to 'HR_Staff'. What is the issue?
options: The user's password has expired
The user is not a member of the specific security group that has NTFS permissions for that folder
The folder is encrypted with BitLocker
The server is out of licenses

fix.q: How do you resolve this according to standard onboarding procedures?
options: Add Sarah's individual user account directly to the folder's security tab
Add Sarah to the 'HR_Staff' security group in Active Directory
Share the folder with 'Everyone'
Disable NTFS permissions on the File Server

tickets.title: USB Storage Capacity Error
tickets.summary: A user is trying to copy a 5GB database export to a 16GB USB drive. The drive is empty, but Windows returns an error saying 'The file is too large for the destination file system.'

triage.q: The drive has enough space, but the file won't copy. What property should you look at first in Disk Management?
options: The drive letter assigned to the USB
The File System type (FAT32, NTFS, or exFAT)
The brand of the USB drive
The color of the USB port (2.0 vs 3.0)

diagnosis.q: Why does a 5GB file fail to copy to a 16GB FAT32 volume?
options: The USB is corrupted
FAT32 has a maximum individual file size limit of 4GB
Windows 10 does not support USB drives larger than 4GB
The file is infected with a virus

fix.q: How do you enable the user to carry this 5GB file?
options: Compress the file into five 1GB parts
Reformat the USB drive as NTFS or exFAT
Buy a 32GB USB drive
Update the USB drivers in Device Manager

tickets.title: Workstation Trust Relationship Failure
tickets.summary: A user returning from a 3-month leave tries to log in to their desktop. They receive the error: 'The trust relationship between this workstation and the primary domain failed.'
artifact: Network: Cable is plugged in; pings to the DC work

triage.q: What tool can you use to verify the status of the computer's secure channel with the domain?
options: Test-ComputerSecureChannel in PowerShell
Disk Cleanup
Device Manager
Task Manager

diagnosis.q: What happened to this computer's account while the user was away?
options: The user forgot their password
The computer password (machine account) in AD is out of sync with the local machine
The computer's hard drive is failing
The monitor resolution is unsupported

fix.q: How do you most effectively fix the trust relationship?
options: Reinstall Windows
Unjoin the computer from the domain and rejoin it
Reset the user's password in AD
Tell the user to log in with a local guest account

tickets.title: Folder Inheritance Discrepancy
tickets.summary: The Marketing Manager created a sub-folder called 'Campaign_2024'. Even though the department has access to the parent 'Marketing' folder, no one can see the new sub-folder.
artifact: User View: Folder does not appear in the directory listing

triage.q: When looking at the 'Security' tab of the 'Campaign_2024' folder, you notice the checkmarks are solid black (explicit) rather than grey (inherited). What does this mean?
options: The folder is a shortcut
Permission inheritance has been disabled for this folder
The folder is read-only
The folder is owned by the SYSTEM account

diagnosis.q: Why did the department lose access when the sub-folder was created?
options: The server rebooted
By disabling inheritance, the folder stopped receiving the 'Allow' permissions from the Marketing parent folder
Marketing users are not allowed to see folders with '2024' in the name
The folder was moved to a different drive

fix.q: How do you restore access to the department correctly?
options: Re-enable inheritance on the 'Campaign_2024' folder to pull permissions from the parent
Give the 'Everyone' group Full Control
Delete the folder and ask the manager to try again
Move the folder to the user's Desktop

tickets.title: Duplicate Computer Object in Active Directory
tickets.summary: You are trying to join a new laptop to the domain with the name 'LAPTOP-05', but you get an error saying 'The account already exists' or 'Access is Denied'.
artifact: AD Search: A computer object named 'LAPTOP-05' already exists in the 'Computers' OU
Status: The existing object was last active 2 years ago

triage.q: What is the first thing to check in Active Directory Users and Computers (ADUC)?
options: Check for an existing computer object with the same name
Check if the user has a valid email address
Check the DHCP lease for the laptop
Check the laptop's serial number

diagnosis.q: Why is AD blocking the domain join?
options: The laptop is too new for the domain
A stale computer object with the same name exists, and the current machine cannot overwrite the existing secure SID
The domain is full
The laptop is running Windows Home edition
Rename the laptop to something unique (e.g., LAPTOP-05B) or delete/reset the old AD object before joining
Disable the antivirus on the laptop
Reboot the Domain Controller
Format the hard drive of the new laptop

tickets.title: Group Conflict: The Deny Rule
tickets.summary: A user, James, is in the 'Contractors' group (Deny Access to Finance) and the 'Project-A' group (Allow Access to Finance). He cannot access the Finance folder.
artifact: Group 1: Contractors (Permissions: Deny Read/Write on Finance)
Group 2: Project-A (Permissions: Allow Read on Finance)

triage.q: When assessing multiple groups, how does Windows handle a 'Deny' vs an 'Allow'?
options: Allow always wins
Deny always takes precedence over Allow in NTFS logic
They cancel each other out
The most recent group added wins

diagnosis.q: Why is James blocked even though he is in a group that is 'Allowed'?
options: Because he is a Contractor
The explicit 'Deny' on the Contractors group overrides any 'Allow' from other groups
His account is locked
The Finance folder is hidden

fix.q: How do you give James access while keeping him in both groups?
options: Remove the 'Deny' entry and simply leave the 'Allow' box unchecked for the Contractors group
Delete the Project-A group
Make James a Domain Admin
Share the folder with James's personal Gmail account

tickets.title: Partition Management for Developers
tickets.summary: A developer wants a separate D: drive for their code, but the PC only has one large C: drive with 500GB of free space.

triage.q: Which Windows tool allows you to resize partitions without losing data?
options: Disk Management (diskmgmt.msc)
Device Manager
System Information
File Explorer

diagnosis.q: What action must be taken on the C: drive before a D: drive can be created?
options: Delete the C: drive
Shrink the C: volume to create 'Unallocated Space'
Format the whole disk
Change the drive letter of C: to D:

fix.q: What are the steps to fulfill the request?
options: Right-click C: -> Shrink Volume -> Enter 102400MB -> Right-click Unallocated Space -> New Simple Volume
Plug in an external drive
Copy all files to a cloud drive and delete the OS
Reinstall Windows and choose two partitions

tickets.title: Network Share vs File System Permissions
tickets.summary: A user has 'Full Control' on the Share permissions of a folder, but they get 'Access Denied' when trying to save a file. The NTFS permissions are set to 'Read Only'.

triage.q: When accessing a file over the network, which permission set does Windows apply?
options: Only Share permissions
Only NTFS permissions
The most restrictive combination of both
The least restrictive combination of both

diagnosis.q: Why is the user unable to save files?
options: The share is broken
The NTFS 'Read' permission is more restrictive than the Share 'Full Control' and becomes the effective permission
The user is not logged in
The file is too large

fix.q: How do you fix this so the user can save files over the network?
options: Update the NTFS permissions to 'Modify' or 'Full Control'
Remove the Share permissions
Map the drive using a different letter
Disable the firewall

tickets.title: New Hardware: The Uninitialized Disk
tickets.summary: A user plugged in a secondary internal SSD, but it doesn't show up in File Explorer (This PC).
artifact: Disk Management: Disk 1 is 'Unknown, Not Initialized, Unallocated'
File Explorer: Only C: drive is visible

triage.q: If a disk is physically connected but not appearing in File Explorer, what status would you expect in Disk Management?
options: The disk marked as 'Offline' or 'Not Initialized'
The disk marked as 'Healthy (Primary Partition)'
The disk missing entirely
A 'No Disk' error

diagnosis.q: Why is the drive invisible to the user?
options: It is a fake drive
A new drive must be 'Initialized' and have a volume created before Windows can assign a drive letter
The SATA cable is upside down
The user doesn't have a license for a second drive
Initialize the disk (GPT), create a New Simple Volume, and format it as NTFS
Reinstall the SSD
Return the SSD to the manufacturer
Update the BIOS

tickets.title: Authentication Block: Kerberos Time Skew
tickets.summary: A user cannot log in to the domain. The error says 'There is a time and/or date difference between the client and the server.'

triage.q: What is the maximum allowed time skew for Kerberos authentication in a Windows Domain?
options: 1 minute
5 minutes
30 minutes
1 hour

diagnosis.q: Why does the time difference block the user from logging in?
options: Windows doesn't like tardiness
Kerberos uses timestamps to prevent replay attacks; a skew larger than 5 minutes causes security rejection
The CMOS battery is dead
The user is in the wrong time zone

fix.q: How do you fix this at the command line?
options: Run 'w32tm /resync' or 'net time \\DCName /set /y' to align the clock
Manually type the time in the system tray
Buy a new clock for the office
Disable Kerberos on the Domain Controller
